- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the low-end of the range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 2–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- After a strong upward spike (forecast > 80.0), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.36 to -0.08), model should adjust downward by 3–5% in next 3–5 days, even if price is still rising.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 82.0 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- When sentiment is flat (±0.05) and forecast is > 80.0, apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid false momentum.
